---
title: "Find a twin"
subtitle: "Choose a school and find the schools in England most like it in intake and setting, then the look-alikes that do better on absence, attainment or value added."
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "site_helpers.R"))
AC <- readRDS(here::here("data", "absence_causes.rds"))
V <- load_va()
L <- AC$local$schools
w <- va_wide(V)
# Each school against similar schools in its own authority, 2025/26
# (the national absence models' school-level residuals, as %)
rs <- AC$resid |> filter(outcome %in% c("overall", "unauth")) |>
  transmute(URN, outcome = paste0("r_", outcome), r = 100 * (exp(r_2526) - 1)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = r)
ADM <- c("SEL" = "Selective", "OTHER NON SEL" = "Non-selective",
         "NON SEL IN HIGHLY SEL AREA" = "Non-selective, selective area")
d <- L |>
  left_join(w |> select(URN, lad, gor_name, att8, att8_dis, att8_non, va_all = va_shrunk_all, va_dis = va_shrunk_disadvantaged,
                        va_non = va_shrunk_non_disadvantaged,
                        l4, run_by, ofsted_latest, lat, lon), by = "URN") |>
  left_join(rs, by = "URN") |>
  left_join(readRDS(here::here("data", "school_context.rds")) |> select(URN, run_by_nat), by = "URN") |>
  mutate(run_by = coalesce(run_by, run_by_nat)) |>
  transmute(URN, n = SCHNAME, la = as.character(la), lad = coalesce(lad, as.character(la)),
            rg = as.character(region),
            fsm, ks2 = ks2_c, eal, wbri, mobile, girls, sen = sen_sup, ehcp, semh, l4z = z_l4, l4,
            pupils = round(exp(size)), size,
            adm = unname(coalesce(ADM[as.character(ADMPOL_PT)], as.character(ADMPOL_PT))),
            sixth = ifelse(sixth, "Has a sixth form", "11-16"),
            place = as.character(place), faith = ifelse(faith, "Religious character", "None"),
            gov = as.character(mat), run_by, ofsted = ofsted_latest,
            overall, illness, unauth, persistent, severe, r_overall, r_unauth,
            att8, att8_dis, att8_non, va_all, va_dis, va_non, lat = round(lat, 4), lon = round(lon, 4)) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double) & !c(lat, lon), ~ round(.x, 3)))
# ---- matching weights: what matters for each measure ------------------------
# Each characteristic is weighted by how much it moves the measure across
# schools: the standard deviation of its fitted contribution in a regression
# of the measure on all the matching characteristics (log for absence).
# Value added and Attainment 8 take their weights from the Attainment 8
# model, since value added is itself what is left once intake is allowed for.
MNUM <- c("fsm", "ks2", "eal", "wbri", "mobile", "girls", "sen", "ehcp", "semh", "l4z", "size")
MCAT <- c("place", "adm", "sixth", "faith")
contrib <- function(y) {
  dd <- d |> mutate(.y = y) |> filter(!is.na(.y), if_all(all_of(c(MNUM, MCAT)), ~ !is.na(.x)))
  m <- lm(reformulate(c(MNUM, MCAT), ".y"), data = dd)
  list(sd = apply(predict(m, type = "terms"), 2, sd)[c(MNUM, MCAT)], r2 = summary(m)$r.squared)
}
norm_w <- function(s) round(pmax(s / mean(s), 0.05), 3)       # mean 1; nothing quite ignored
FITS <- c(lapply(c(overall = "overall", illness = "illness", unauth = "unauth", persistent = "persistent",
                   severe = "severe"), function(o) contrib(log(d[[o]] + 0.1))),
          list(att8 = contrib(d$att8)))
W <- lapply(FITS, function(f) as.list(norm_w(f$sd)))
W$r_unauth <- W$unauth
W$va_all <- W$va_dis <- W$va_non <- W$att8_dis <- W$att8_non <- W$att8
W$combo <- as.list(norm_w((unlist(W$overall) + unlist(W$att8)) / 2))
W_R2 <- sapply(FITS, `[[`, "r2")

# ---- over time: value added by year, absence by year --------------------------
vy <- va_years(V)
VA_YEARS <- sort(unique(vy$year_label))
va_arr <- function(g) {
  a <- vy |> filter(group == g) |> mutate(year_label = factor(year_label, VA_YEARS), va = round(va, 2)) |>
    tidyr::complete(URN, year_label) |> arrange(URN, year_label) |>
    group_by(URN) |> summarise(ys = list(va), .groups = "drop")
  a$ys[match(d$URN, a$URN)]
}
d$va_y <- va_arr("all"); d$vd_y <- va_arr("disadvantaged"); d$vn_y <- va_arr("non_disadvantaged")
AB <- readRDS(here::here("data", "absence_change.rds"))
AB_TP <- sort(unique(AB$series$tp))
cid_of <- AB$series |> distinct(URN, cid)
ab_arr <- function(o) {
  a <- AB$series |> transmute(cid, tp = factor(tp, AB_TP), v = round(.data[[o]], 2)) |>
    tidyr::complete(cid, tp) |> arrange(cid, tp) |> group_by(cid) |> summarise(ys = list(v), .groups = "drop")
  a$ys[match(cid_of$cid[match(d$URN, cid_of$URN)], a$cid)]
}
d$ab_o <- ab_arr("overall"); d$ab_u <- ab_arr("unauth")
eng_ab <- list(overall = round(AB$trend$overall[match(AB_TP, AB$trend$tp)], 2),
               unauth = round((AB$trend$`Unauthorised holiday` + AB$trend$`Other unauthorised`)[match(AB_TP, AB$trend$tp)], 2))
prov <- VA_YEARS %in% (vy |> filter(provisional) |> pull(year_label))

# Areas: each school sits in a region, a local authority and a district
areas <- list(region = sort(unique(d$rg)), la = sort(unique(d$la)), district = sort(unique(d$lad)))
payload <- list(schools = d, areas = areas, gy = yl(max(V$spec$years)),
                weights = W, va_years = yl(VA_YEARS), va_prov = prov,
                ab_years = yr(AB_TP), eng_ab = eng_ab, built = format(Sys.Date(), "%d %B %Y"))
```

::: {.callout-note}
## How to use it

1. **Choose a school.** Pick a region, local authority or district, then a
   school within it.
2. **Choose what to match on.** Matching uses intake and setting only, never
   results or attendance. By default it weights what matters most for the
   measure you choose.
3. **Closest twins** are the schools most like yours anywhere in England.
4. **Anti-twins** are the look-alikes, from the 50 (or 25, or 100) most
   similar, that do furthest *better* than yours on the measure you choose:
   - lower absence of a kind;
   - higher value added or Attainment 8;
   - or absence and value added together.

Click a twin, in the chart, on the map or in the table, to compare its fact
card with your school's, including value added and absence year by year.
**Print for governors** gives a clean copy of the comparison for a meeting. The address bar
keeps your choice, so a link takes someone else to the same comparison.
:::

```{r payload}
#| output: asis
cat("<script>window.TWINS = ", jsonlite::toJSON(payload, dataframe = "rows", na = "null", auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 3),
    ";</script>\n", sep = "")
```

## How the matching works {#sec-how}

Every school is described by the characteristics the
[absence models](absence_causes.qmd) use, in groups you can switch on or off:

- **Pupils:** disadvantage (FSM), KS2 prior attainment, EAL, White British,
  joining mid-phase, and the share of girls.
- **Needs:** SEN support, EHC plans, and social, emotional and mental health
  need.
- **Neighbourhood and place:** neighbourhood education, and rural or urban.
- **The school:** size, admissions, sixth form, and religious character.

For each measured characteristic, the difference between two schools is
taken in standard deviations, capped at three. For each category, it is 0
if they match and 1 if not. The average across the characteristics is the
distance, and *similarity* is one minus it, as a percentage. This is a form
of Gower's distance, as in the original project's twin finder.

**Weighting.** By default each characteristic is weighted by how much it
matters for the measure you chose. A school that matches yours on what
drives that measure counts as more alike than one that matches on what
does not. The weight is how much the characteristic moves the measure
across schools: the standard deviation of its part in a regression of the
measure on all the characteristics (log absence for absence). The weights
are scaled to average one. Value added and Attainment 8 both take the
Attainment 8 weights. Value added is already what is left once intake is
allowed for, so the twins should match on what drives results. The
combined measure takes the average of the overall absence and Attainment 8
weights. You can switch to equal weights.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-weights
#| tbl-cap: "Matching weights by measure (average 1), and how much of each measure the characteristics explain between schools (R²)."
WL <- c(fsm = "Free school meals", ks2 = "KS2 prior attainment", eal = "EAL", wbri = "White British",
        mobile = "Joined mid-phase", girls = "Girls", sen = "SEN support", ehcp = "EHC plans",
        semh = "Social, emotional and mental health need", l4z = "Neighbourhood education", size = "Size",
        place = "Rural or urban", adm = "Admissions", sixth = "Sixth form", faith = "Religious character")
ML <- c(overall = "Overall absence", illness = "Illness", unauth = "Unauthorised", persistent = "Persistent",
        severe = "Severe", att8 = "Results (Attainment 8, value added)")
wt <- sapply(names(ML), function(o) unlist(W[[o]])[names(WL)])
tb <- rbind(as.data.frame(wt) |> mutate(across(everything(), ~ sprintf("%.2f", .x))),
            sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * W_R2[names(ML)]))
rownames(tb) <- c(unname(WL), "R² of the model")
colnames(tb) <- unname(ML)
kt(tb, align = "rrrrrr") |>
  kableExtra::row_spec(nrow(tb), italic = TRUE)
```

Similar intake is not the same as identical circumstances. A twin can
differ in what the data does not see: its pupils' health, its community,
its buildings, its staffing. An anti-twin that does much better is a reason
to ask what it does differently, not proof that copying it would work.

**Data.** The data for each kind of measure is:

- **Absence:** autumn and spring 2025/26.
- **Characteristics:** the January 2026 school census and SEN data.
- **Results:** Attainment 8 for `r payload$gy` and Value Added v2.1 over
  2021/22 to 2024/25, shrunk, each for all, disadvantaged and
  non-disadvantaged pupils.
- **Absence against similar schools:** within the school's own authority,
  as on the [absence page](absence_causes.qmd#sec-school).
- **Over time:** each year's value added against England (unshrunk; the
  latest year provisional), and absence in the autumn and spring terms from
  2016/17, followed through academy conversion and changes of trust as on
  [How school absence changes](absence_change.qmd).

All of it is published school-level data.
